## 🎯 What this dataset is

Each row is **one smart meter during one 30-minute interval**. It holds what the meter reported, facts about the meter and its home, the weather, the state of the electric line it sits on, and the **correct answer** about whether the reading can be trusted.

Most rows are healthy. Some come from meters that are drifting, stuck, corrupted or **falsified**. Others come from **genuine grid events** (outages, voltage sags, cable faults) where the data is correct even though it looks abnormal.

The main prediction task: **can the data coming from this meter be trusted, and if not, why?**

> ⚠️ **All data is simulated.** No real STEG meter data is included. Baselines are calibrated on public Tunisian figures, and every anomaly was injected on purpose, so the labels are exact.

## 🚀 Quick start

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("energymind_full_joined.csv.gz", parse_dates=["timestamp"])

gt_cols   = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("gt_")]       # 15 answer columns
simulator = ["annual_kwh_target", "fault_weight"]                # simulator settings, not meter fields

X = df.drop(columns=gt_cols + simulator)                         # model inputs (50 columns)
y = df["gt_data_trustworthy"]                                    # main target: 1 = trust, 0 = faulty/falsified

# time-based split (a random split would leak seasonality)
train = df[df.timestamp <  "2025-09-01"]
valid = df[(df.timestamp >= "2025-09-01") & (df.timestamp < "2025-11-01")]
test  = df[df.timestamp >= "2025-11-01"]

# 0.2% of rows have no measurements (communication loss) and an empty target
train = train.dropna(subset=["gt_data_trustworthy"])
```

## 🧩 Column groups

| Group | # | Columns | Role |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 🕒 Identifiers | 4 | `timestamp`, `node_id`, `feeder_id`, `meter_id` | keys |
| 🔌 Meter measurements | 10 | `energy_kwh` … `meter_event_code` | **inputs** |
| 🏠 Meter details | 21 | `phase` … `fault_weight` | inputs (2 are simulator settings) |
| 🌦️ Weather and calendar | 6 | `temp_c` … `is_ramadan` | inputs |
| 🧭 Feeder context | 11 | `n_meters_total` … `energy_balance_gap_pct` | inputs |
| 🏷️ Ground truth | 15 | all `gt_*` | labels and evaluation only |

### 🛡️ Keep the answers out of the model

| Role | Columns | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **Inputs** (50) | everything except `gt_*` and the two simulator settings | what a model may see |
| ⚙️ **Simulator settings** (2) | `annual_kwh_target`, `fault_weight` | drop them; real meters do not report these |
| 🟡 **Labels** | `gt_data_trustworthy`, `gt_label`, `gt_subtype`, `gt_event_id`, `gt_expected_response` (+ optional `gt_feeder_*`, `gt_n_meters_*`) | targets and scoring |
| 🔴 **Oracle** | `gt_true_energy_kwh`, `gt_true_voltage_v`, `gt_metering_discrepancy_kwh`, `gt_tech_loss_kwh`, `gt_streetlight_kwh` | clean physical values no real system can know. Use them only to analyse errors and check explanations, **never as inputs**. |

## 📖 Column dictionary

### 🕒 Identifiers

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `timestamp` | Start of the 30-minute interval, local time |
| `node_id` | Neighborhood: `N1`, `N2`, `N3` |
| `feeder_id` | Low-voltage line, e.g. `N1-F2` |
| `meter_id` | Smart meter, e.g. `N1-M014` |

### 🔌 Meter measurements (what the meter *reports*)

| Column | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `energy_kwh` | kWh | Energy imported from the grid in the interval. May be corrupted or falsified. |
| `pv_export_kwh` | kWh | Solar energy sent back to the grid (0 for homes without PV) |
| `reactive_kvarh` | kvarh | Reactive energy (mostly motors such as AC compressors) |
| `voltage_v` | V | Mean voltage, nominal 230 V; 0 means supply is cut |
| `voltage_min_v` | V | Lowest voltage in the interval (reveals short sags) |
| `voltage_max_v` | V | Highest voltage in the interval (reveals swells) |
| `current_a` | A | Mean current |
| `power_factor` | – | Real ÷ apparent power (0.55–1.0); blank when supply is lost |
| `thd_v_pct` | % | Voltage distortion; the usual limit is 8% |
| `meter_event_code` | – | Meter's own log: `none`, `power_fail`, `power_restore`, `voltage_sag`, `voltage_swell`, `cover_open`, `magnetic_tamper` (rare false alarms included) |

### 🏠 Meter details (fixed per meter, repeated on every row)

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `phase` | Electrical phase L1–L3 |
| `customer_class` | `res_small`, `res_medium`, `res_large`, `small_commercial` |
| `dwelling_type` | `apartment`, `villa`, `shop` |
| `floor_area_m2`, `occupants` | Home size and number of people (0 for shops) |
| `distance_to_transformer_m` | Cable distance to the transformer (longer means lower voltage) |
| `lat`, `lon` | Synthetic coordinates near the neighborhood centre |
| `has_ac`, `ac_units`, `ac_unit_kw` | Air conditioning present, number of units, power per unit |
| `has_pv`, `pv_kwp` | Solar panels present, and size in kWp |
| `has_electric_heater`, `has_electric_water_heater` | Electric heating flags |
| `meter_install_year` | Year of installation (older meters fail more often) |
| `comm_tech` | `PLC`, `GPRS` or `NB-IoT` (PLC loses data most) |
| `meter_model`, `meter_accuracy_class` | Model label and accuracy class (1.0 means ±1%) |
| `annual_kwh_target` | ⚙️ Yearly consumption the simulator aimed for |
| `fault_weight` | ⚙️ Simulator weight for picking this meter for sensor faults |

### 🌦️ Weather and calendar

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `temp_c`, `humidity_pct` | Outdoor temperature and humidity at the node |
| `ghi_wm2` | Solar irradiance (drives PV output) |
| `is_weekend` | Saturday or Sunday |
| `is_public_holiday` | Tunisian public holiday |
| `is_ramadan` | Ramadan period (consumption shifts to suhoor and iftar) |

### 🧭 Feeder context (measured at the head of the line by an accurate meter)

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n_meters_total`, `n_meters_reporting` | Meters on the feeder, and how many reported this interval |
| `feeder_kwh_net` | Energy through the feeder head (includes line losses and street lighting) |
| `feeder_voltage_v`, `feeder_current_a`, `feeder_thd_pct` | Voltage, per-phase current and distortion at the feeder head |
| `frequency_hz` | Grid frequency (about 50 Hz; dips mean a generation problem) |
| `sum_meters_import_kwh`, `sum_meters_export_kwh` | What the customer meters add up to |
| `energy_balance_gap_kwh`, `energy_balance_gap_pct` | Feeder head minus customers. About 5% is normal; a larger gap suggests theft or biased meters; a negative gap suggests inflated readings. |

### 🏷️ Ground truth (`gt_*`)

| Column | Role | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gt_label` | 🟡 label | One of 7 classes (see Labels) |
| `gt_subtype` | 🟡 label | The exact cause, e.g. `fdi_scale`, `gain_drift`, `outage` |
| `gt_event_id` | 🟡 label | Identifier of the injected event, e.g. `N1-EV012`; all rows of one event share it (`none` if normal) |
| `gt_data_trustworthy` | 🟡 label | 1 = trustworthy, 0 = faulty or falsified, blank = no data |
| `gt_expected_response` | 🟡 label | Suggested handling: `auto_log`, `auto_correct`, `notify_operator`, `human_decision` |
| `gt_true_energy_kwh` | 🔴 oracle | Clean energy before meter error and injection |
| `gt_true_voltage_v` | 🔴 oracle | Clean voltage before injection |
| `gt_feeder_label`, `gt_feeder_subtype`, `gt_feeder_event_id` | 🟡 optional | The same labels for the feeder as a whole |
| `gt_tech_loss_kwh`, `gt_streetlight_kwh` | 🔴 oracle | True line losses and street-lighting energy on the feeder |
| `gt_metering_discrepancy_kwh` | 🔴 oracle | True minus reported energy on the feeder (the part caused by drift, theft or corruption) |
| `gt_n_meters_falsified`, `gt_n_meters_sensor_fault` | 🟡 optional | Meters on the feeder that are falsified or faulty in this interval |

## 🏷️ Labels

The central idea: **a real grid event and a data problem can look alike but need opposite responses.**

```
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  abnormal-looking ───► │ Is the DATA correct?         │
  reading               └───────┬──────────────┬───────┘
                           yes  │              │  no
                                ▼              ▼
                    GENUINE PHYSICAL EVENT   DATA PROBLEM
                    grid_event               sensor_fault
                    equipment_failure        data_corruption
                    (trust the data,         falsification
                     act on the grid)        (distrust the data, fix the meter)
                                             comm_loss (no data at all)
```

| `gt_label` | `gt_subtype` values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **normal** | `none`, `minor_gap` | Healthy reading (or a 1–2 interval missing value) |
| **grid_event** | `outage`, `load_shedding`, `voltage_sag`, `voltage_swell`, `demand_surge`, `cold_load_pickup` | Genuine event, correctly recorded |
| **equipment_failure** | `cable_fault`, `transformer_degradation`, `transformer_trip`, `cold_load_pickup` | Genuine natural equipment failure |
| **sensor_fault** | `gain_drift`, `bias_step`, `voltage_offset_drift`, `clock_shift`, `stuck_value` | Degraded or biased sensor |
| **data_corruption** | `spike_gain`, `negative_value`, `saturation`, `unit_error_x1000` | Transmission or firmware corruption |
| **falsification** | Physical tampering: `partial_reduction_bypass`, `selective_bypass`, `meter_zeroing`. Data-only (cyber): `fdi_scale`, `fdi_replay`, `fdi_evasion`, `fdi_inflate`, `coordinated_fdi` | Manipulated readings |
| **comm_loss** | `comm_dropout_burst` | All measurements missing for 1.5–48 hours |

## 💉 What was injected

| Label | Subtype | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| grid_event | `outage` | Supply = 0 on a feeder or the whole node, then a post-restoration surge (×1.6, then ×1.25) |
| | `load_shedding` | Scheduled rolling cut of 1.5–2 h on one feeder, July–August peaks |
| | `voltage_sag` | Mean voltage −15…−45 V; minimum dips a further 40–110 V |
| | `voltage_swell` | Mean voltage +8…+22 V |
| | `demand_surge` | Feeder load ×1.35–1.8 for 1.5–4 h, summer evenings |
| equipment_failure | `cable_fault` | Meters beyond a cut point lose supply; upstream meters stay on |
| | `transformer_degradation`, `transformer_trip` | Voltage ramps down, distortion and losses rise, ends with a trip |
| sensor_fault | `gain_drift` | Slow gain error, mostly under-reading; labelled once it reaches 1% |
| | `bias_step` | Constant gain ×0.86–0.93 or ×1.07–1.14 for 3–11 weeks |
| | `voltage_offset_drift` | Voltage sensor offset ramps to ±4…11 V |
| | `clock_shift` | All channels delayed by 1–3 hours |
| | `stuck_value` | Last value repeated for 3–48 h |
| data_corruption | `spike_gain` | Energy ×8–40 |
| | `negative_value` | Sign flip |
| | `saturation` | Energy fixed at 99.999 kWh |
| | `unit_error_x1000` | Wh reported as kWh |
| falsification | `partial_reduction_bypass` | Energy **and** current ×0.4–0.8 (physical bypass) |
| | `selective_bypass` | Reduced only in selected hours |
| | `meter_zeroing` | Energy and current forced near 0 for 5–8 h on about 35% of days |
| | `fdi_scale` | Only the energy field scaled ×0.3–0.75 |
| | `fdi_replay` | Energy replaced by the value from the same half-hour a week earlier |
| | `fdi_evasion` | Scaling factor wanders as a random walk to mimic natural variance |
| | `fdi_inflate` | Energy ×1.35–2.0 (framing a victim) |
| | `coordinated_fdi` | 3 meters on one feeder scaled over the same window |
| comm_loss | `comm_dropout_burst` | Missing values; PLC meters most exposed |

**Why detection is not trivial (deliberate):**
- A **real event hits neighbors together**; a **failing sensor is isolated**.
- **Physical tampering** keeps `energy ≈ voltage × current × power factor × 0.5 h` consistent but opens the **feeder energy-balance gap**. **Data-only FDI** breaks that consistency but leaves voltage untouched.
- **Drift** is smooth and slow, **bias** is a constant step, and **theft** is hour-selective and sometimes leaves a tamper log.
- **Hard negatives are included**: summer vacations (genuinely low use), the Ramadan pattern shift, heat-wave surges, PV export reversing the current, and post-outage surges.
- Rows are labelled **only when the anomaly is visible**: a drift once it reaches 1%, a selective bypass only in the bypassed hours.

## 🏗️ How the data was made

1. **Weather** for three Tunisian climates (coastal, interior, southern coast), with heat waves and solar irradiance.
2. **Household load** with Saturday–Sunday weekends, public holidays, Ramadan (suhoor and iftar peaks), summer vacations, temperature-driven air conditioning, electric heating, and rooftop PV with export.
3. **Calibration** so residential consumption matches the STEG average of about 1,450–1,470 kWh per year.
4. **Electrical model**: voltage drops along each feeder, rises with PV export, power factor falls with AC load, and meters add small measurement noise.
5. **Feeder meter** that sees true energy plus line losses and a small unmetered street-lighting load, which creates the realistic ~5% balance gap.
6. **Genuine events** injected first, then **data problems and falsification** at meter level.
7. **Row-by-row labelling** and a final **join** into this single table.

Generation uses a fixed random seed (2025), and each neighbourhood has its own random stream, so N1 is the same whether or not N2 and N3 are generated. The generator is in `simulate/` and reproduces the committed file exactly (every value of all 67 columns):

```bash
cd simulate
python inject_anomalies.py --out ../build --seed 2025          # stages 1-2: healthy network + injected anomalies (~35 s)
python join_dataset.py --data ../build/data --out ../build/energymind_full_joined.csv.gz   # stage 3: one table
```

`generate_baseline.py` (stage 1) can also be run alone to write an anomaly-free version of the three neighbourhoods. Every figure quoted from the dataset is reproduced by `scripts/check_dataset.py`.

## ✅ Realism checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Residential annual consumption (STEG average ≈ 1,450–1,470 kWh) | N1 **1,475** · N2 1,354 · N3 1,764 kWh per year (N2 and N3 differ by design) |
| Summer vs. winter (homes with AC) | July–August ≈ **1.66×** January–February; homes without AC 0.79× |
| Voltage on normal rows | mean **231.4 V**; 1st–99th percentile 219–237 V; 0.0006% outside the EN 50160 band (207–253 V) |
| Energy vs. voltage × current × power factor × time | median error **0.93%**, 95th percentile 2.7% |
| Feeder energy-balance gap on clean intervals | median **5.0%** (5th–95th percentile 1.8–9.5%) |
| Frequency on normal rows | 49.95–50.05 Hz |

## 📏 Reference baselines

Simple detectors, run only to show the data is learnable but not trivial (node N1, labels used for scoring only):

| Baseline | Result |
|---|---|
| Isolation Forest (unsupervised), flag untrustworthy data | ROC-AUC **0.757**; top-7% alerts: precision 0.34, recall 0.46, false-positive rate 4.8% |
| Isolation Forest, flag genuine events | ROC-AUC 0.706 |
| Physics rule: 7-day median of energy ÷ (V·I·PF·t) outside [0.88, 1.12] | recall 0.31, false-positive rate **0.31%** |

- **Easy (recall ≥ 0.85):** spike, saturation and unit-error corruption, voltage-offset drift, and most data-only FDI (`fdi_scale`, `fdi_inflate`, `coordinated_fdi`, `fdi_evasion`).
- **Moderate (0.3–0.45):** `bias_step`, `stuck_value`, `fdi_replay`.
- **Hard (recall ≤ 0.1):** `gain_drift`, `clock_shift`, `negative_value`, `selective_bypass`, `partial_reduction_bypass`, `meter_zeroing`, `transformer_degradation`. These need comparison with neighboring meters, the feeder balance and time context.

---

## 🧪 Suggested evaluation

- **Split by time** (train Jan–Aug, validate Sep–Oct, test Nov–Dec) and check that each fault type you care about appears in every split; some types have only 2–3 events in the year.
- **Unsupervised models** can train on `gt_label == "normal"` rows only.
- **Metrics**: precision, recall, false-positive rate; response latency (time of first alert minus the start of the event, using `gt_event_id`); per-event recall; calibration of confidence scores against `gt_data_trustworthy`.
- **Explanation quality**: define a checkable rule, for example that the top evidence feature agrees with the true cause in `gt_subtype`.
- **Report per subtype**, not only overall, because an overall score hides faults that are never caught.

### Suggested response policy (`gt_expected_response`)
A starting point to test escalation logic, not a standard.

| Response | Applied to |
|---|---|
| 🟢 `auto_log` | load_shedding, voltage_sag, demand_surge, cold_load_pickup |
| 🔧 `auto_correct` | stuck_value, all data_corruption, comm_loss of 12 intervals or less |
| 🔔 `notify_operator` | outage, voltage_swell, clock_shift, voltage_offset_drift, longer comm_loss |
| 🧑‍🔧 `human_decision` | all falsification, gain_drift, bias_step, all equipment_failure |

---

## ⚠️ Limitations

- **Synthetic data.** A detector tuned here may overfit the generator's recipes. Test on a real dataset before claiming real-world performance.
- **Few events per type.** Many falsification and sensor-fault subtypes have only 2–4 events in the year, so per-type results are statistically thin.
- **Anomaly share (~6.8%) is higher than in real life**, chosen so models have enough examples.
- **Assumed meter fields.** An IEC-style half-hourly profile with min/max voltage and an event log was assumed; real STEG meters may report differently.
- **Weather is statistical**, not reanalysis data, and **air conditioning** accounts for about 55% of summer energy in AC homes, below the ~70% press figure for Tunisia.
- **Calendar dates** for Ramadan, Eid and other lunar holidays are approximate (±1 day).
- **One transformer per node**; no three-phase imbalance. **Coordinates are synthetic.**
- **Empty cells are intentional**: about 0.2% of rows have no measurements (communication loss), and voltage-related fields are blank or zero while supply is cut.
